observation.visible_scene: A calm, narrow body of water (pond or slow stream) framed by dry golden reeds in the foreground and brown grassy hills rising on both sides under a clear deep-blue sky. A large leafless tree with a thick trunk and sprawling bare branches stands rooted in the middle of the water, its trunk and branches mirrored on the surface; faint snow-dusted peaks are visible in the left background gap between hills. The composition is wide and landscape-oriented.
visible_changes: The overall framing, hill silhouettes, horizon, tree trunk and main branches stay in fixed positions across all sampled frames, indicating a static camera with no pan, tilt or zoom.

The water surface shows gentle, slowly evolving ripples: the bright sky-reflection patches and the dark vertical streaks of the tree's reflection shift, break up and re-form subtly from frame to frame, indicating continuous small-amplitude surface motion rather than a change in the objects themselves.
The reflection of the bare tree in the water remains present throughout; it wavers with the ripples but does not appear or disappear.

Foreground reeds and the thin twigs against the sky show at most very slight positional variation between frames, consistent with a near-still scene; no large or clearly trackable movement of these elements is confirmed.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the slight water motion or any twig movement is caused by wind is not shown in the clip.
The state of the scene before t=0 and after t=2.67 s is outside the excerpt and cannot be judged; the segment is an arbitrary window, not a start or end of any action.
uncertain_details: Any sway of the thin upper branches and foreground grasses is at the limit of resolution and cannot be reliably distinguished from compression noise, so it is treated as possible but unconfirmed.
Because the background is fixed, camera motion is judged absent, but minute drift cannot be fully excluded from these sparse samples.
